language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello! My name is Bernard Thys and I work for the cruise ships which leave from here, at the Port of Zeebrugge. This is a large port in Belgium at the edge of the North Sea. One of my duties is to make sure all the passengers on the ship have enough drinking water.
This got me interested in learning more about drinking water and I am excited to share what I've learned with you.

I used to wonder why we could not drink all this sea water directly. I then understood that drinking water comes mainly from two sources: groundwater and surface water. And both types of water need to be cleaned before drinking.
I’m going to tell you about dirty water and how to clean it. Let’s begin!
This is going to be important!

exercises.title: Point and Nonpoint Sources of Water Pollution

dialog.text: Drinking water needs to be clear and not smelly. Water might have bits of solids and germs in it. Water is polluted from many sources. Pollution sources are of two types: Point Sources and Nonpoint Sources.
A Point source means you can say exactly where the pollution came from. For example, the waste of a particular factory.

Most pollution comes from people’s daily activities. This is called Nonpoint source pollution, because we cannot pinpoint exactly where the pollution came from. For example: storm drain water which contains leaves and oil.
Let’s sort the following into Point Sources or Nonpoint Sources.

You know, I have made my own water filters at home. I construct them using bottles and layers of different materials. When making a water filter it is important that the layers should begin with the larger pieces on top and the finer pieces below.
By doing this, the larger pieces of dirt are filtered out first and the finer ones filter out later.

Here I am going to show you a few filters. Can you help me arrange
them correctly?

activities.subtitle: Ultraviolet (UV) light passed through water kills microbes. What could be the main problem with a UV filter?

answers.text: Water should be clear, not muddy: else the light will not reach the microbes.
Water should not have any solid pieces because the UV light cannot get rid of them.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Distillation is boiling the water and collecting the steam in a clean container. Which water would you distill?

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Boiling water kills 99.9% of all living organisms. When is it best to boil water?

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Chemicals like chlorine are used to purify water. What should you be careful about?

answers.text: Make sure you add the right amount of chemicals: not too much, not too little.
Make sure that the chemicals don't make the water taste bad.

outro.text: Awesome! Now you know four additional methods of water purification!
